title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline), implemented as paired difference in success rates per the preregistration (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001; preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a308...). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable misconfigurations) is not supported given the observed baseline error prevalence. All principal artifacts, provider-call accounting, validation traces, and analysis CSVs are archived with SHA-256 digests and are referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can translate operator intent into device-specific configuration quickly, but incorrect commands risk outages. A common operational safeguard is to place a deterministic validator between model output and device application and to permit bounded automated repairs. Although many proposals argue for validators, rigorous preregistered quantification of their marginal effect under a bounded-adapter contract (single hosted model, bounded repair attempts) is lacking with forensic artifact traceability. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a308...) to ask: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types remain after automated repairs? We adopted a paired estimand (within-task comparison) to control for task difficulty heterogeneity and enforced an adapter contract to bound repair budget and provider-call semantics.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and runtime checking (e.g., header-space analysis and VeriFlow) provide canonical pre-deployment checks and inspired our deterministic validator design [Kazemian et al.; Khurshid et al.]. Recent NetOps work explores LLM-driven intent→configuration translation (NetConfEval and others) but frequently omits preregistration, cryptographic artifact hashing, or bounded-adapter semantics. Our study differs in being preregistered, paired, adapter-constrained (single repair attempt), and fully artifact-hashed to permit forensic replication and auditing. We follow recommendations to prefer operationally meaningful tasks and verifier-assisted GVR architectures rather than generic LLM knowledge benchmarks.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. We froze the study plan before execution (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001; SHA-256 = 5cb8a308...). Primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, computed per task as guarded_success − baseline_success where success = 1 − actionable_error. Algebraic mapping: actionable_error_rate = 1 − success_rate; therefore an absolute decrease in actionable-error rate equals the observed increase in success_rate (guarded − baseline). For our run: baseline_success_rate = 199/200 = 0.995, guarded_success_rate = 200/200 = 1.000, absolute paired difference = 0.005. The preregistered confirmatory test was an exact McNemar two-sided test supplemented by a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) as implemented by paired_binary_analysis_v1 (analysis artifacts archived).
sections.results: Execution and accounting. Execution completed planned_episode_count = 400 (200 tasks × 2 conditions) with completed_episode_count = 400 and failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}, matching model_calls_used = 201 (execution manifest: execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e2..., raw results SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). Scoring was deterministic: the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parsed responses into canonical ASTs, applied intent-constraint and dependency/workflow checks, and produced per-episode binary scores (0/1) and validation_before/validation_after traces; representative per-episode JSONs and their SHA-256 digests are archived under execution/scoring/ (examples included in the evidence bundle).
sections.discussion: Primary paired outcome (artifact-grounded). The confirmatory paired analysis (complete_pair_count = 200) yielded baseline_success_count = 199 and guarded_success_count = 200; contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba...) shows n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1 (guarded-only improvement), n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI for absolute paired difference = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Why H1 is not confirmatory under preregistered power assumptions. The preregistration targeted an absolute reduction of 0.15 (15 percentage points) during power planning; this assumed a much higher baseline actionable-error rate than observed. The observed baseline actionable-error rate = 1 − 0.995 = 0.005 (1/200), so a 50% relative reduction corresponds to an absolute reduction of 0.0025 (0.25 percentage points), far smaller than the effect scale used in the a priori power calculation. Therefore the preregistered confirmatory design lacked sensitivity to validate small relative improvements under the low-error regime actually observed.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-hashed paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a bounded adapter contract. On the synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline produced a small absolute improvement (1 → 0 actionable errors; absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect hypothesis is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence was substantially lower than assumed during power planning. All principal artifacts, provider-call accounting, per-episode validator traces, and analysis CSVs are archived and referenced below to enable auditors to reproduce contingency tables, stratified counts, and the exact discordant episode identifier from the authoritative execution artifacts.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Reviewer-required per-vendor stratified counts and the explicit discordant episode identifier are not included verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle text; auditors can compute them from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02), but we do not invent or assert specific per-vendor numbers or an episode id in the manuscript where those values are not present verbatim in the provided archive.
